articles.headline: Real Madrid conspiracy claims dismissed as a 'smokescreen' by LaLiga president
articles.description: LaLiga president Javier Tebas has called claims of a refereeing conspiracy against Real Madrid "a smokescreen to hide other shortcomings" after the team's defeat to Atletico Madrid in Sunday's derby.
articles.body:
LaLiga president Javier Tebas has called claims of a refereeing conspiracy against Real Madrid "a smokescreen to hide other shortcomings" after the team's defeat to Atletico Madrid in Sunday's derby.

Coach José Mourinho said Madrid were denied "two clear red cards" in the game at the Metropolitano -- bringing a printout of photos of the incidents to his post-match news conference -- and alleged referee Miguel Ortiz Arias "couldn't cope with the pressure" of the high-profile fixture due to a lack of experience.

"I don't want to say this was prepared -- I want to think they were mistakes," Mourinho said, after a result which left Madrid six points behind Barcelona in the title race, adding that "if they let us compete on an even playing field, there's a long way left."

Tebas, who has frequently clashed with Madrid and club president Florentino Perez, commented on the debate on social media on Tuesday, while sharing an article which claimed "Real Madrid's enemies" were responsible for the team's struggles in LaLiga.

"The usual mouthpieces and the regime-aligned media are already spinning the same old narrative: the permanent conspiracy, Tebas posted on X. "When it isn't the Negreira case, it's the referee; or else, the complaint is that the official isn't an international-level referee."

"To maintain that referees are conspiring against Real Madrid is to live in another galaxy," Tebas continued. "That narrative serves as a smokescreen to hide other shortcomings that are plain to see in these opening matches of the season. It is easier to point to a conspiracy than to explain what is actually happening on the pitch.

"A refereeing error does not prove a conspiracy, nor does repeating the claim for years make it true. TIME TO TAKE OFF THE BLINDERS! It is only September, and they are already claiming the league is tainted. No one with common sense buys that old excuse anymore."

With seven games played, Madrid are already six points behind Barcelona, after losing at Real Betis and then in Sunday's derby.

- Atlético Madrid 2-1 Real Madrid: Grimaldo and David down 10-man visitors

- Jonathan David winner helps Atlético Madrid down Real Madrid

By contrast, Barça have maximum points, having scored 31 goals in seven matches.

Spain coach Luis de la Fuente -- who agreed a contract extension until 2032 on Monday -- was asked about the controversy on radio station Cadena Ser.

"I don't believe any of that," De la Fuente said, when asked about suggestions of a conspiracy. "If I believed in that, in such manipulation, I'd be better off going home, or we all would. And if someone believes it and has proof, then they should present that proof.

"But if we thought that, what would be the point? What would we be doing here? We'd just be wasting our time. That isn't my attitude towards life, or towards sport. I've lost, sometimes a lot, and I've won at other times. And I've never thought there was some hidden hand pulling the strings.

articles.headline: Orioles' Pete Alonso reaches 40 home runs on son's birthday
articles.description: Orioles slugger Pete Alonso threw a birthday bash for son Teddy as he turned 1, changing his walk-up music and hitting home runs Nos. 39 and 40 in a victory vs. Toronto.
articles.body:
Baltimore Orioles slugger Pete Alonso threw a birthday bash for son Teddy as he turned 1 on Monday, changing his walk-up music and, for the icing on the cake, hitting home runs Nos. 39 and 40 in a 4-3 victory against the Toronto Blue Jays.

Sept. 21 will be a day and night for the Alonso family to remember, indeed.

For starters, Alonso and his wife Haley began the day with a celebration at home, complete with presents and a large "Happy Birthday Theodore" banner.

Once he got to the ballpark, Alonso got right to work in the first inning. After walking from the batter's box to the plate to Dire Straits' "Money for Nothing," per normal, Alonso blasted No. 39 to right field.

He changed his tune in the eighth inning, however. In a one-time exception to celebrate Teddy, Alonso asked for "September" from Earth, Wind & Fire to be played.

Alonso then launched a two-run blast to become the first Orioles player since Anthony Santander in 2024 to reach 40 home runs in a season.

"That's for him. That's his birthday song," Alonso told reporters. "Sick. It's 100% special, Hopefully, we can bookmark this game. I know it doesn't matter now, because he's not going to understand it for a couple years. But hopefully, a couple years down the line, I can kind of look back and just kind of bookmark this and keep it for the archives, and then hopefully, he appreciates it one day."

Alonso leads the American League with 108 RBIs.

"His baseball card, his accolades, the track record is there," manager Craig Albernaz said. "Hitting 40 home runs and having over 100 RBIs in this league is really impressive and the consistency he does it, that doesn't happen by accident. Just all the work he puts in behind the scenes."

With a new team and a newborn son, Alonso admitted it took some time this season to get into his usual rhythm.

"I think the hardest thing was navigating parenthood. It's like, 'How do we get this down?' Being husband, being dad, and then also being ready to my maximum capabilities by first pitch," Alonso said. "Just a couple routine tweaks, and I feel like as the season has gone on, I feel like I've just been able to kind of refine that and get more and more in tune and in rhythm.

"Really thankful for my teammates sticking with me. Really thankful for my wife."

articles.headline: Fantasy football buzz: Loss of Dart filters down to rest of Giants' skill-position players
articles.description: Jaxson Dart's injury has a cascading effect on the Giants, whose skill players would also take a hit.
articles.body:
Everything that happens in the NFL has additional context when viewed from a fantasy football perspective. From position battles to injuries and so much more, the news cycle will constantly affect player values in fantasy football.

Our fantasy football buzz file, with contributions from our ESPN fantasy writers and our NFL Nation reporters, aims to provide fantasy managers with the intel they need as news breaks around the league.

Sept. 22: Giants take a hit with loss of Jaxson Dart

By Michael F. Florio

Jaxson Dart suffered a knee injury on the New York Giants' opening drive Monday against the Los Angeles Rams, spoiling the night early for the Giants. While we await official word, Giants GM Joe Schoen told the broadcast that Dart "was going to be OK. ESPN NFL Nation reporter Jordan Raanan posted on X that Dart wanted to return to the game before the team shut him down. Additionally, Dart was able to walk off on his own power and spent the second half on the sideline in street clothes.

All of the Giants take a fantasy hit if Dart misses time.

Wide receiver Malik Nabers caught one of his four targets Monday night for just one yard. He avoided an injury scare (shoulder) himself and was able to play 76% he snaps, a big jump from the 53% he played in Week 1. While we have yet to see the WR1 upside we know Nabers possesses, he would be more of a volatile WR2 -- potentially WR3, depending on the matchup -- without Dart. Tight end Isaiah Likely had 10 targets, catching five for 33 yards. That volume keeps him in play as a rock-solid TE1.

The only other fantasy-relevant Giants player without Dart would be running back Cam Skattebo, who turned 16 opportunities into 55 yards. The volume shows that he is an RB2 for fantasy purposes, but his floor and ceiling is lower without Dart. Skattebo gets a bounce-back opportunity next week against the Tennessee Titans.

Quarterback Jameis Winston is the next man up for the Giants, but he struggled mightily against the Rams. He is purely in play in superflex leagues, and even there he is ideally more of a QB3 for depth.

The Rams looked like the Rams again on "Monday Night Football". Matthew Stafford played like an MVP, throwing for 327 yards, four touchdowns and one interception. He is a QB1 most weeks, but with the Denver Broncos on tap next week, he is a little more option-dependent.

Wide receiver Davante Adams was the star of the night with Puka Nacua sidelined. Adams caught eight of 10 targets for 195 yards and two touchdowns. The future Hall of Famer is in play weekly, but he is a must-start any time Nacua is out.

Both of the Rams' RBs balled out. Kyren Williams played 55% of snaps, with 12 carries, 14 routes and two targets, turning that work into 97 yards and a touchdown. Blake Corum played 45% of snaps, with 12 carries, seven routes, one target and 92 scrimmage yards. articles.headline: How active NFL players continue to redefine all-time sack list
articles.description: Myles Garrett's torrid pace up the all-time sack list paces seven active players making their moves among the greats.
articles.body:
Last season, defensive end Myles Garrett won his second Defensive Player of the Year award after setting the NFL's single-season record with 23 sacks with the Cleveland Browns.

This season, he'll continue his climb up the NFL's all-time sack list as a member of the Los Angeles Rams after a blockbuster trade in June -- making the Rams favorites to win the Super Bowl, according to DraftKings Sportsbook, heading into the season.

Garrett entered the season with 125.5 career sacks, which was tied for 20th in NFL history and third among the other six active players -- Von Miller (No. 9), Cameron Jordan (No. 17), Calais Campbell (No. 25), T.J. Watt (No. 26), Danielle Hunter (tied for No. 27) and Khalil Mack (T-29th) -- in the top 30. 

Joining the top 30 soon could be Aaron Donald, who un-retired to join Garrett on the Rams' defensive line. Donald's 111 sacks currently sits two behind 30th. 

As for Garrett, he entered his 10th season in the NFL averaging approximately 14 sacks per season. If he were to replicate that production, he would tie Pro Football Hall of Famer Jason Taylor, who currently sits at No. 7 all-time. If Garrett were to have another historic season, he would surpass Michael Strahan (No. 6) and approach top-five all-time territory.

Miller, who signed with the Dallas Cowboys in August, can also pass Strahan in his 15th season -- as he sits only three sacks behind him.  

But Garrett's 125.5 career sacks were 10.5 more than any other player since his rookie season in 2017, according to ESPN Research, heading into the seaosn. The pass rusher recorded at least 14 sacks in each of the past five seasons, the longest such streak by any player since 1982.

If Garrett has 18.5 or more sacks this season, he will hold the record for the most over a two-season span since 1982, according to ESPN Research, and his current ascension up the all-time list ranks as the second-fastest pace among the top five all time behind only Reggie White. 

As we look at how the sack list is redefined this season, we'll highlight milestones across the NFL landscape

We will update this file as the active players move up, and we'll add nuggets and milestones throughout the season.

Week 2 update

The second week of the season saw little movement near the top of the all-time list, but Watt's hot start continues, with the defensive end recording 1.5 sacks to now put him at 3.5 through two weeks (No. 2 in the NFL this season) and break a tie with Campbell to move to 25th. 

Hunter (27th) and Mack (29th) also recorded 1 sack over the weekend to break ties and move up one spot on the list. 

Donald (33rd) made his season debut on "Monday Night Football" against the Giants after taking two years off. He finished with three tackles, one for a loss, but did not record a sack.

articles.headline: Paul Skenes says WBC contributed to velocity drop in 2026
articles.description: Pirates ace Paul Skenes, whose season has been marked by an uncharacteristic dip in velocity, cited the World Baseball Classic as a source of his struggles this year.
articles.headlineJa: ポール・スキーンズ、2026年の球速低下はWBCが一因と明かす
articles.descriptionJa: 今季らしくない球速低下が目立つパイレーツのエース、ポール・スキーンズは、今年苦戦している原因としてワールド・ベースボール・クラシック（WBC）を挙げた。
articles.body:
Pittsburgh Pirates ace Paul Skenes, whose season has been marked by an uncharacteristic dip in velocity, cited the World Baseball Classic as a source of his struggles this year.

Skenes discussed his disappointing 2026 season with the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette, saying that the WBC was "kind of the root" of the diminished velocity that plagued him in recent months.

"There are a lot of other factors, so I don't want to put everything on [the WBC]," Skenes told the Post-Gazette as part of a wide-ranging interview published Monday. "But I feel like that was kind of the root of it a little bit."

Skenes' average fastball velocity this season was 96.8 mph, down from 98.1 mph last season and 98.8 mph in 2024.

The three-time All-Star's four-seam fastball dropped to a career-low 95.7 mph in a start last month against the Miami Marlins and averaged just 96.1 mph in his most recent start Friday against the Kansas City Royals.

Although he acknowledged mechanical adjustments that also contributed to his performance, Skenes mentioned the impact that the early-March WBC had on his annual ramp-up routine.

"Usually, that time of year, you're kind of ramping up and it's a little bit slow," he told the Post-Gazette. "You can kind of get onto the slope and find your body. One live [batting practice], you're topping at 97, and then the next you're 98, 99.

"And that wasn't the case this year. ... Looking back, I don't think that really helped."

Skenes, 24, is 10-11 with a 3.91 ERA and has 192 strikeouts in 168 innings over 31 starts this season. He won the National League Cy Young Award last year, when he boasted a major-league-best 1.97 ERA, and was the NL Rookie of the Year in 2024, when he had a 1.96 ERA.

Skenes revealed that he didn't feel 100% mechanically even early this season, when he was still posting his usual dominant numbers -- including a 1.09 ERA during an eight-start stretch in April and May.

"Even then, I didn't feel like I had my delivery," he said. "It's just weird. It's easier to kind of put your finger on it after the fact than it is in the moment."

Skenes said he expects to regain his mechanics ahead of the 2027 season. He emphasized that he doesn't regret representing Team USA, but added that the WBC "affected" his season with the Pirates.

"It definitely affected the year," he said. "Unfortunately, I don't think I'm the only one. ... Yeah, I don't know. [The WBC] definitely didn't make things easier."

articles.headline: Benjamin Šeško vows to 'fully dedicate' himself to recovery after Man United injury setback
articles.description: Manchester United striker Benjamin Sesko has vowed to "fully dedicate" himself to his recovery from an ongoing shin issue.
articles.headlineJa: マンUで怪我に見舞われたベンヤミン・シェシュコ、回復に「全力を尽くす」と誓う
articles.descriptionJa: マンチェスター・ユナイテッドのストライカー、ベンヤミン・シェシュコは、続いているすねの傷みの回復に「全力を尽くす」と誓った。
articles.body:
Manchester United striker Benjamin Šeško has vowed to "fully dedicate" himself to his recovery from an ongoing shin issue.

The 23-year-old moved to Old Trafford from RB Leipzig last August in a deal worth 76.5million euros (£66.3m/$88.6m) plus 8.5m euros (£7.4m/$9.9m) in potential add-ons.

Šeško scored 12 goals during a promising first campaign that was brought to an abrupt end by a shin injury in May, which ruled him out of all of United's preseason friendlies.

The striker managed to play a part in the first six games of the season, scoring twice, only for the recurrence of shin pain to rule him out of Sunday's 1-1 draw at Fulham and international duty with Slovenia.

"I am very sorry that I will have to miss the next matches of the national team," Sesko posted on Instagram.

"I have always played for Slovenia and will always play with heart and pride. The most important thing now is to fully dedicate myself to recovery.

"I am already working on getting back on the field as soon as possible and helping the national team and the club again.

"I believe in our boys, and I am sure that they will show the team spirit that has always adorned us this time.

"I can't wait to be able to wear the jersey with the national emblem again and, until then, I will be Slovenia's biggest fan."

Slovenia host Scotland on Saturday and end the three-week international break with a trip to Hampden Park, with a home clash against North Macedonia and a trip to Switzerland in between, as the Nations League gets under way.

United are not back in action until Oct. 10, when fellow strugglers Tottenham head to Old Trafford, before tough-looking trips to Atletico Madrid, Leeds and Como.

- Kylian Mbappé on past Liverpool transfer talks: 'Mum went to Anfield and fell in love'

- Cole Palmer, Declan Rice withdraw from England's Nations League squad

Šeško's absence for those matches would be a major blow given Michael Carrick's side failed to sign another out-and-out striker during the summer.

Asked whether United should have done so, given the current situation, the head coach said after the Fulham match: "No, I think that just because you get setbacks in certain positions, you can't sign a player for cover in every one.

"We're not sure with Ben yet, he felt some pain after the game [against Brighton in the Carabao Cup] and we are assessing him at the moment.

"He definitely wasn't ready for [Sunday]. I haven't got any more news to give you, just that he felt pain on his shin."

Šeško is one of four United players to have withdrawn from international duty. Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford pulled out of the England squad, while Karl Darlow did not not join up with Wales.

The Premier League club said: "Each of the players will be assessed and undergo individual recovery plans during the current three-week international break."
